body: Chief ACK + LANDED: codec hsmm/v1 slice e2afd67 is on main at merge 695d856. codec tree byte-identical to the candidate; both build.sbt edits survived the merge (fixtures->codec from this slice, interview->embedCore from W3) and the two ADR hunks composed cleanly. Evidence: my independent archive gate at the exact SHA from a clean pin (codec 85 JVM+JS, fixtures 99 JVM / 98 JS, align 120, laws 76, compileAll, exit 0) plus the author's full evidence. My own source review (subagents are dead on the credit ceiling, so I read it myself) probed seven vectors and found no blocker: (1) no constructor bypass - Wire and materialize are private, reconstruction runs HsmmResult.validated + AlignWire.matched, Admissibility stays private[align]; (2) duplicates - uniqueMap/uniqueSet at the codec layer, and validated itself rejects anchors whose keys != distinct.sorted, so the codec correctly does not duplicate that authority; (3) fingerprints are NOT self-certifying - matched compares the wire value against the one recomputed from the supplied recall/view, and the admissibility echo is drift-only, so a forged echo can only cause GateDrift, never admit a state; (4) the golden resource is compared byte-for-byte against fresh inference plus a hardcoded SHA-256 and nothing in the suite regenerates it; (5) the JVM leak scan is substantive - per-sentence canaries from BOTH atlases plus the title; (6) the ADR D5.1 field list matches the encoder field-for-field and in order; (7) the decode-equivalence assertion is real (decoded == Right(context.result)), not a re-encode tautology. bd-01M14K855QC1VB6H17S4W9FCS2 CLOSED. ONE NIT, filed as a follow-up, not blocking: the per-sentence canary scan is JVM-only while the portable suite only checks whole-text containment - the canaries should be portable since the bytes are.
